title: Give the Agent a Budget, Not a Token — Sachin Malhotra, Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic CI engineer describes replacing boolean token scopes with a four-dimensional 'budget' for agents: asymmetric verbs (only grant verbs that fail loudly), refilling rate limits on every write, trip wires that page humans on aggregate anomalies, and an 'undo test' to size all three. Enforcement must live in a proxy that stamps the agent's identity, not in prompts or caller-supplied headers.

takeaways.technique: Asymmetric verbs: grant only fail-loudly operations
takeaways.what_they_do: Classify each agent action by whether its failure surfaces on a dashboard (unskip test, page human) vs fails silently (skip test, delete); agents get the loud-failing verbs, humans keep the silent ones.
Every write gets a per-caller, per-resource-kind, per-namespace cap per time window that refills automatically; bypass flag refuses to work inside agent sessions and tells the agent to ask a human.
takeaways.evidence_quote: inside a cloud code session or inside an agent session effectively the the bypass flag simply refuses to do anything

takeaways.technique: Trip wires on aggregates, not per-call allow lists
takeaways.what_they_do: Track one aggregate metric per agent behavior (e.g. investigation threads launched per hour per failure signature); page a human when it deviates from baseline, then fix with one sentence in the agent's context file.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we track one number uh which is the number of investigation threads that our agent is launching per hour

takeaways.what_they_do: For each write ask: can the agent roll it back itself, and is the blast radius acceptable? If either is no, require a second key held by someone else plus an audit record.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the agent can effectively roll back its own change and the blast radius is acceptable to you, you effectively log it and you let it go

takeaways.technique: Identity stamped by proxy, not caller
takeaways.what_they_do: A per-session proxy holds real credentials and stamps every outbound call with the agent's known identity; downstream systems (quotas, rate limits, approvals) key on that stamp, and child jobs inherit it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with the proxy in the path, the agent never gets to say who it is. The proxy already knows

takeaways.technique: Text for intent, infra for enforcement
takeaways.what_they_do: Policy lives in two layers: markdown context files explain the why (~80% compliance) and a deterministic proxy enforces the hard rule with 403s; prompt injection cannot talk past the proxy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It works about 80% of the time... text can shape the intent but there is no enforcement anywhere
